column1: # Shiren GB — THE GLOSSARY. 391 item, monster, appearance and NPC names.
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS, AND WHY IT IS FROZEN
# `こんぼう` is an item name, a line of help text, a combat message and a shop's dialogue.
# Translated batch by batch it becomes Club / Cudgel / Stick, and review cannot catch that
# -- catching it means holding 1,263 strings in your head at once. So the names are
# translated ONCE, here, and every later batch takes them as a constraint.
# `tools/lint_en.py --glossary` enforces it: if a Japanese string contains a glossary
# term, the English must use the frozen rendering.
#   * Names read as modern official Shiren English -- plain and meaning-first -- rather
#     than as the Aeon Genesis SNES romanisations. `ひとつめゴロシ` is "One-Eye Killer",
#   * The CATEGORY nouns are Aeon Genesis', so the two projects agree where it is cheapest
#     for them to: Herb / Bracer / Staff / Pot / Scroll. (`~/Documents/Workplace/Shiren/
#   * A tier family reads as a family: Rat Minion / Rat Boss / Rat Kingpin.
#   * Proper nouns that carry no meaning in Japanese either stay transliterated --
# SERIES TERMINOLOGY AUDIT, 2026-08-10. Monster/NPC names now prefer an exact Japanese
# match from the newest official English Shiren release represented by the Mystery Dungeon
# Franchise Wiki, then Shiren 1 DS, then an established unflagged Moonlight Village wiki
# name. Wiki entries explicitly marked unofficial are not silently adopted; unresolved
# differences live in script/term_uncertainties.tsv. The Shiren 2 fan-patch list is the
# next authority when an exact official term does not exist.
# VWF BUDGET RESET IN PROGRESS (2026-08-09). See VWF_BUDGETS.md.
#   class item, appearance -> legacy ITEM_CAP source/substitution guard: 16 chars
#   class monster, npc     -> legacy NAME_CAP source/substitution guard: 14 chars
# These are NOT Dot Gothic pixel limits. A combat line and its runtime name still share a
# 144px canvas, but the old 14/16 numbers were carried forward from fixed-width cells
# without remeasuring every substitution path. `lint_en.py --glossary` keeps them as a
# conservative engineering-review guard while that census is open. If a proposed name
# crosses one, do not shorten it automatically: measure its menu suffix variants and every
# runtime template, then widen/fix the source path or choose wording on actual evidence.
# THE CURRENT ITEM-LIST CONTRACT IS SEPARATE. The proportional payload owns 128px and its
# source scanner currently accepts at most 18 glyphs, including runtime status suffixes.
# `True Rapier+99` leaves comfortable pixel and allocator headroom; the wider guard stays
# in place so another long equipment name plus a native status mark cannot silently fall
# Staff/pot `[NN]` and every signed equipment value remain mandatory audit variants; do not
# judge a bare name or assume `99` is the widest pair in a proportional font.
# DUPLICATE JAPANESE IS NORMAL AND MUST STAY DUPLICATE. `くねくねハニー`, `オロチ`,
# `いやしウサギ`, `ばくだんウニ`, `ぼうれいむしゃ` and `エーテルもどき` each appear at
# two or three tiers with the same name in Japanese; they keep one English name. What the
# collision check forbids is the reverse -- two DIFFERENT Japanese names landing on the
# same English, which would make two monsters indistinguishable in a message.
# `New Weapon 3` and friends are unused placeholder slots (`しんきぶき3` = 新規武器3).
# They are named rather than left Japanese so that a slot leaking on screen is legible.
